clue.text: Rather Conservative? Well done!

parts.note: rather, as in 'fairly', means quite
the political right is the conservative side

explanation.surface: Someone praises a fairly Tory remark with a hearty 'Well done!'.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of hearty approval, much like 'Absolutely correct!', said when someone has acted properly.

clue.text: Horrid to see such a dangerous customer

definitions.meaning: unpleasant to look at, unsightly
a nasty, threatening person is called this kind of customer

explanation.surface: A menacing customer is unpleasant to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsightly in appearance, and also threatening or hostile, as in a nasty customer.

clue.text: Your sum wrong, you'll get it in the neck

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of sum are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: A teacher warns that a botched calculation will bring a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get it in the neck' suggests punishment, but here it points to a gland in the neck; 'you'll get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A gland located at the base of the neck, in the upper chest, so a thing found in the neck.

clue.text: Went down and repaired lawn, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a patchy lawn is repaired by sowing it again with grass seed

explanation.surface: Someone's garden lawn shrank and was then patched up.
explanation.definitionFit: Water or a hairline that retreated has drawn back, gone down.

clue.text: Keep talking, fool

definitions.meaning: a phrase urging a speaker to continue
a silly person, an idiot

explanation.surface: Someone tells an idiot to carry on speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Two words meaning 'continue' run together give a slang term for an idiot.

clue.text: Author contributed lots new to play

indicators.note: new says the letters of lots are made over into a fresh order

parts.note: to play with something is to toy with it

explanation.surface: A writer gave a great deal to the drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' looks like a stage drama but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace is a famous author.

clue.text: Outcome of seabed mapping shows net profit

definitions.meaning: charting the sea floor would produce a line of the bottom
the final figure on an account after costs, the result

explanation.surface: Charting the ocean floor turns out a tidy profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounting jargon for the final profit figure, playfully read as a line traced along the sea floor.

clue.text: Tramp-direction for his eviction from garret?

definitions.meaning: a homeless, destitute person

definitions.text: direction for his eviction from garret?
definitions.meaning: to leave an attic room you go first downstairs and then outside

explanation.surface: A vagrant is told how to leave his attic.
explanation.definitionFit: A destitute vagrant, and also the instruction to go downstairs then outdoors from an attic.

clue.text: Nothing on record showing company em, blem

parts.note: a log is a written record, as a ship's log
nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A firm's emblem is described as showing nothing on the record.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means after, so O follows LOG.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm's trademark symbol is its identifying design, the emblem printed on its products.

clue.text: Kindergarten for aspiring actors?

parts.note: a nursery for small children read whimsically as a training ground for people who perform in dramas

explanation.surface: A nursery is pictured as a drama academy for budding thespians.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursery for preschool children, where young ones learn through games, is pictured as a training academy for the stage.

clue.text: Brown, naturally

parts.note: a browning of the skin that comes from nature, namely from sunlight rather than a bottle

explanation.surface: Something is described as brown by nature.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin darkened by exposure to sunshine is brown in a natural way, not dyed or painted.

clue.text: Drinks may be served on this ship

definitions.text: Drinks may be served on this
definitions.meaning: a small mat that a glass is set down on
a vessel that sails along the coast from port to port

explanation.surface: Drinks are served aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinks mat protects a table under a glass, and a small trading vessel hugs the coastline; both carry the same name.

clue.text: Assume gear appropriate for hill-climbing

parts.note: reads like putting on walking kit for the hills but means a driver shifting to a lower gear for a steep slope

explanation.surface: A hiker puts on boots suitable for the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver shifts into a lower gear when climbing a steep gradient.

clue.text: Prosecutor's attitude in case?

parts.note: a lawyer's stance at trial, read also as a grammatical case for the object of a verb

explanation.surface: A barrister's stance during a court trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A prosecutor's manner is one of laying blame, and in grammar this is the case of the direct object.

clue.text: Vex, seizing fine plunder

indicators.note: seizing means the word for vex holds the letter for fine within it

parts.note: to vex is to annoy, to rile
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: An official angers people by grabbing a fine to loot.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransack and steal from a place is to plunder it.

clue.text: Individual effort by Scotsman, a wise chap

parts.note: a solo is a performance or effort by one person alone
mon is the Scots form of man

explanation.surface: A Scot's lone achievement marks him out as a sage.
explanation.walkthrough: The biblical King Solomon is proverbial for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The Old Testament king is so famed for wisdom that his name means a sage.

clue.text: Look, rates have changed

indicators.note: changed tells us the letters of rates are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone notices that interest rates have moved.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze fixedly is a long, steady look.

clue.text: Little song in sailor's bag

definitions.meaning: a short simple tune with words
a small bag in which a seaman keeps sewing kit and odds and ends

explanation.surface: A short tune is tucked inside a seaman's kitbag.
explanation.definitionFit: A short simple song shares its name with the small kit bag a seaman uses for needles and thread.

clue.text: Parts of circle in a catholic society

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic

explanation.surface: Segments of a circle are found within a Catholic association.
explanation.definitionFit: Curved portions of a circle's circumference are its segments of curve.

clue.text: Somewhat squalid old pool

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather dirty, ancient swimming pool.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air public swimming bath, a pool for bathing, is called by this Italian-derived name.

clue.text: Look angry as Elgar is ruined

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so the composer's name is broken up and reformed

explanation.surface: A music lover scowls because Elgar's work has been spoilt.
explanation.definitionFit: To glower is to give a fierce, hostile stare, looking angrily at someone.

clue.text: Grenade injured VIP

indicators.note: injured means the word grenade is damaged and its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A bomb has hurt an important person.
explanation.definitionFit: A high-ranking nobleman, originally Spanish, is a very important person.

clue.text: Keeping regular hours

definitions.meaning: making level or smoothing out
the time of day between afternoon and night

explanation.surface: Someone keeps sensible, regular times.
explanation.definitionFit: Making something level, and also the late part of the day after work.

clue.text: Be furious and try to get thin

parts.note: to have a go is to try, so try means go
spare as an adjective means lean or thin

explanation.surface: Someone is angry and attempting to lose weight.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'go spare' is British slang for losing one's temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A British slang idiom for becoming wildly angry, to lose one's temper.

clue.text: It's clear I'd enter the race

indicators.note: enter says the letters for I'd go into the word for a race

parts.note: a race is a sporting event
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone declares plainly that they would sign up for the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obvious or plain to see is easily seen, apparent to everyone.

clue.text: A fair car, certain to be a hit

definitions.meaning: a small electric bumper car at a funfair
read as 'dodge them', the challenge when bumping is sure

explanation.surface: A fairground vehicle is guaranteed to be popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper car at a funfair is driven to collide with others, so it is bound to be bumped.

clue.text: Row about foreign character's arrest

indicators.note: about places the noise word around the Greek letter

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din
eta is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A dispute concerns the arrest of a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' here, a noise, not a line or a boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in custody is to take them in, as police do when they make an arrest.

clue.text: Sort of hunt that's a bore

definitions.meaning: a hunt following an artificial scent trail dragged over the ground
something tedious, a tiresome thing

explanation.surface: A certain kind of hunt is tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunt along a laid scent trail, and also a tedious nuisance in slang.

clue.text: Problem afoot with a crop

definitions.meaning: a painful hard patch of skin on the foot
a cereal grain grown in fields

explanation.surface: A farmer has difficulties with the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful lump on a toe, and also grain such as wheat or maize.

clue.text: Amazingly grand lot, in this town

indicators.note: amazingly says the letters are thrown into astonishing disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at how much wealth a certain town holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The town is in County Durham, in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A market town in north-east England, the town the anagram spells out.

clue.text: Wife has greeting this?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies
ave is the Latin greeting 'hail'

explanation.surface: A wife gives a hand gesture as a greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A movement of the hand is a common greeting, and the wordplay builds it from W and a Latin salute.

clue.text: Contract of two hearts?

parts.note: reads like a bridge bid in hearts but means a promise between two lovers to marry

explanation.surface: A bridge player bids two hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal agreement to marry is a pact between two loving people.
